decision.explanation: Retain the separately compiled long-row helper (r349) as local work in progress. Compared with the previously retained bit kernel, the integrated chain takes about 0.7–2.7% less time, and tendon cases generally improve about 0.4–1.7%; some confidence intervals remain uncertain. Hinge and some ball cases are still slower, with central hinge losses around 0.9–1.9%, retained explicitly. No blanket aggregate improvement or final C parity is claimed. The native unpartitioned wide-index build has small chain gains but repeated branch regressions. The local 128-bit preference repeatedly regresses small movement cases and is not adopted; 256-bit was inspected only. The retained row/helper contracts close all 156 checks, and the actual solver caller separately closes 86 obligations under the unchanged callee contracts. All retained C 3.17/C 3.14 validation/release gates pass. The working source has no machine-width attribute, global compiler-flag change, suppressed check, stronger public input condition, assumption or new trusted body.
decision.next_step: Follow the actual C four-double block/tail structure when investigating smaller SIMD groups, with exact frame/rejection contracts and fresh lane/integrated tests. Address the remaining small-model regressions; retain full-port/current-stable alignment, functional dynamics composition and matched-build C performance acceptance as open requirements.
